title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART is placed as the Marco Polo stand-in: Richard died in 1199, some 70 years before the journey, and an English crusader king is the wrong culture and wrong century for a Venetian merchant. Better options existed (a generic Merchant-flavoured unit, a Trade Cart, or a renamed King/heroic unit).
BERSERK x1 in Player Three's 'caravan guards' is a Viking infantry unit with no place on the 13th-century Silk Road; a Militia-line or Camel-line unit would have served.

Player One's escort of KNIGHT x5, CAVALIER x1 and CROSSBOWMAN x5 is a Latin-Christian field army, not a merchant caravan; the Polos travelled with a handful of servants and Mongol safe-conduct, not a Western heavy-cavalry column.
GUARD_TOWER at the Mongol camp is an Imperial-Age fortification more suited to a settled state; Mongol steppe camps of the 1270s were not palisade-and-guard-tower forts.
PIKEMAN x6 guarding the destination (Shangdu) — Yuan garrison troops would be better represented by cavalry archers or spearmen of steppe/Chinese type, not European pikemen.
No TRADE_CART or pack animals are placed anywhere despite the brief insisting 'the caravan's pack animals must survive'; the engine offers trade carts and camels, so this omission is avoidable.

Shangdu, the Khan's summer palace, is represented by a single YURT_A with no palace, wonder, or Chinese/Mongol monumental structure, while the PAVILION_A and MARKET sit with the European player instead.
